SELF-HEALING QUANTUM SENSOR INFRASTRUCTURE AND RECONFIGURABLE MATTER AT THE LIMIT Module Replacement × Calibration Recovery × Service Continuity This exploratory engineering monograph develops a falsifiable research architecture for modular quantum-enabled and classical sensor infrastructure that must continue providing scientifically valid measurements despite component failure, material aging, vendor discontinuity, shared-reference faults and partial loss of maintenance capability. The central question is not whether a network can switch its modules or restart operation. It is whether that network can recover a traceable measurand, independently verify accepted functions, constrain autonomous repair authority and maintain a reliable fallback or retirement path when restoration is impossible or unsafe. The synthesis combines three prior mother architectures while distinguishing inherited methods from unverified integration hypotheses. Swarm Manufacturing and Robotic Matter at the Limit, especially chapters 52–64, contributes modular reconfiguration, robot maintenance, repairability, physical interfaces and quality assurance. Autonomous Quantum Health Infrastructure at the Limit, especially chapters 41–49 and 75–82, contributes fault isolation, graded authority, service recovery, classical fallback and reconstructible handoffs. Self-Calibrating Quantum Biosensing Networks at the Limit, especially chapters 49–64, contributes reference integrity, package drift, calibration recovery, common-mode failure detection and replacement continuity. Those original works are methodological sources, not experimental demonstrations of a finished self-healing quantum–nano infrastructure. The proposed core relation is R_post = (F_verified_after/F_required) × P_trace × P_recover. It is a normalized design heuristic rather than a universal physical law or safety certificate. F_verified_after represents the independently confirmed functions following repair; F_required is the explicitly declared essential service scope. P_trace and P_recover describe traceability and verified recovery, respectively. Their possible statistical dependence, calibration uncertainty, hidden physical wear and categorical scientific or safety vetoes must be evaluated separately. A powered-on replacement cannot count as a successful repair when the old measurand cannot be reconstructed, independent calibration is missing or the new connector causes hidden drift. The research program defines the Replace–Recalibrate–Verify–Rollback protocol. Each event preserves the old reference state, instrument serial number, raw observations, material and connector information, authority, operator identity, calibration uncertainty and independent acceptance results. Two coupled maps—physical module topology and calibration-reference dependency graph—make visible how a local intervention can change network measurement interpretation. The project permits repair, partial restoration, classical fallback, safe service reduction, full replacement and responsible retirement as legitimate possible outcomes. The monograph comprises 82 chapters with 12 separately paginated research units per chapter, 30 concise physics and mathematical derivation plates, one candidate chapter relation and spatial reconfiguration model per chapter, 200 Research Gates and 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos. Every Gate and Embryo is linked to one of 233 numbered equation eggs that draw on recognized relations in probability, mechanics, statistical uncertainty, control and reliability; the equation eggs are not new physical laws. Chapters use a common comparative research grammar, so programmatically counted words should not be confused with an equal quantity of independent scientific discoveries or fully proved theorems. Proposed experiments compare qualified manual replacement, centralized maintenance, fixed spare-node redundancy and distributed robotic repair with a matched classical-only sensing baseline. A module network is challenged through connector damage, alignment drift, thermal fatigue, forged component identity, expired reference artifacts, firmware regressions, power loss and common-mode calibration failure. Blinded replacement batches and independent laboratory replays evaluate scientific recovery and lifecycle burden rather than merely counting restored packets or achieving low machine-learning loss. The Research Gates workbook provides chapter and page navigation, 200 falsifiable studies, 33 provisional Answer Embryos, physics-plate and equation-egg indices, a module replacement register, calibration lineage, fault injection matrix, recovery closeout, human authority, lifecycle economics and three-source continuity. It is intended as an extendable research apparatus for successor investigators, not as evidence that the listed experiments have been performed. SCIENTIFIC AND DEPLOYMENT BOUNDARIES.
